αἰῶνός: αἰών — life, lifetime, life-force; masc. gen. sg., of what is taken away (with εὖνιν): ’of life’
βέλος: βέλος — missile, thing thrown; neut. acc. sg. (here a hurled rock)
γλαφυρῆς: γλαφυρός — hollow, hollowed; fem. gen. sg.
δυναίμην: δύναμαι — be able; pres. opt. 1 sg. mid., in a wish (αἲ γάρ … δυναίμην ’would that I could’)
εἴρηται: εἴρομαι — ask, inquire; aor. subj. 3 sg. (epic, = Attic ἔρηται): ’he asks’
εὐρυμίδης: Εὐρυμίδης — son of Eurymus; patronymic, masc. nom. sg., epic -ης as in Attic
εὔχεαι: εὔχομαι — claim, profess, boast; pres. 2 sg. mid., epic uncontracted (= Attic εὔχῃ): ’you claim’
εὕροι: εὑρίσκω — find; aor. opt. 3 sg., in a wish: ’may he find’
εὖνιν: εὖνις — bereft, robbed (of + gen.); adj., masc. acc. sg., agreeing with σε
θέμωσε: θεμόω (from θέμις) — make so, ordain, drive; aor. 3 sg., unaugmented (= ἐθέμωσε); exact sense disputed
θέσφαθ: θέσφατος — decreed by a god; neut. pl. noun, ’oracles’, elided (θέσφαθ’ = θέσφατα)
κατανεύων: κατανεύω — nod, nod down; pres. part. act. masc. nom. sg.: ’nodding’
κατεγήρα: καταγηράω — grow old; imperf. 3 sg., epic -α (= κατεγήρα, Attic -ᾱ): ’was growing old’
κατερχομένης: κατέρχομαι — come down; pres. part. mid. fem. gen. sg.: ’as it came down’
κεκοτηότι: κοτέω — bear a grudge, be angry; perf. part. act. masc. dat. sg. (epic -ηότ-, = κεκοτηκότι): ’angered’
κελαινεφέι: κελαινεφής — dark with cloud, cloud-wrapped (epithet of Zeus); masc. dat. sg. (= -εῖ)
κιχήσεσθαι: κιχάνω — reach, overtake, befall; fut. inf. mid.: ’to befall’
κοντὸν: κοντός — pole, punting-pole; masc. acc. sg.
κορυφὴν: κορυφή — peak, summit; fem. acc. sg.
κρατερῆφι: κρατερός — strong, mighty; fem. dat. sg. with epic -φι (= Attic κρατερᾷ), instrumental, with βίηφι
κρατὶ: κάρη (κράς) — head; neut. dat. sg. (stem κρατ-): ’with the head’
κρονίδῃ: Κρονίδης — son of Cronos; masc. dat. sg., epithet of Zeus
κυανοπρῴροιο: κυανόπρῳρος — dark-prowed; gen. sg., epic -οιο (= Attic -ου), with νεός
κυανοχαίτης: κυανοχαίτης — dark-haired (epithet of Poseidon); masc. nom. sg. as a noun: ’the dark-haired one’
κυανοχαῖτα: κυανοχαίτης — dark-haired (epithet of Poseidon); masc. voc. sg.
κυκλώπεσσιν: Κύκλωψ — Cyclops; masc. dat. pl., epic -εσσιν (= Attic Κύκλωψι)
κώπῃς: κώπη — oar; fem. dat. pl., epic -ῃς (= Attic κώπαις): ’with oars’
λᾶαν: λᾶας — stone, rock; masc. acc. sg. (Attic λίθος)
μαντευόμενος: μαντεύομαι — prophesy, divine; pres. part. mid. masc. nom. sg.: ’prophesying’
μαντοσύνῃ: μαντοσύνη — art of prophecy, seercraft; fem. dat. sg., dat. of respect: ’in prophecy’
μαρμάρῳ: μάρμαρος — rock, boulder (later ’marble’); masc. dat. sg., with ὀκριόεντι
μειλιχίοις: μειλίχιος — gentle, soothing; masc. dat. pl., with ἐπέεσσιν
νήια: νήιος — of a ship (Attic ναυτικός); neut. acc. pl.: ’ship’s (timbers)’
οἰήιον: οἰήιον — tiller, steering-oar handle (Attic οἴαξ); neut. acc. sg.
οἰκί: οἰκία — dwelling, house; neut. pl., elided (οἰκί’ = οἰκία)
οἰμώξας: οἰμώζω — wail, groan aloud; aor. part. act. masc. nom. sg.: ’having groaned’
πέμψαι: πέμπω — send, convey; aor. inf. act.: ’to send’
παλαίφατα: παλαίφατος — spoken long ago; neut. pl., agreeing with θέσφατα: ’long-ago-spoken’
περιμήκεα: περιμήκης — very long; masc. acc. sg., epic uncontracted (-εα = Attic -η)
πεῖθον: πείθω — persuade; impf. 3 pl., unaugmented (= ἔπειθον): ’were persuading’ (οὐ … ’did not persuade’)
πλημυρὶς: πλημυρίς — flood-tide, swell; fem. nom. sg.: ’the surge’
ποιήσας: ποιέω — make, render; aor. part. act. masc. nom. sg.: ’having made (him)’
πρήσσοντες: πρήσσω — accomplish, traverse (Attic πράττω); pres. part. act. masc. nom. pl.: ’making our way over’
προπεσόντες: προπίπτω — fall forward; aor. part. act. masc. nom. pl.: ’throwing themselves forward’
πτολιπόρθιον: πτολιπόρθιος — sacker of cities (Attic πτολίπορθος); masc. acc. sg., epithet of Odysseus
πόντονδε: πόντος — sea; masc. acc. sg. + directional -δε: ’seaward, into the sea’
σχέτλι: σχέτλιος — reckless, cruel; masc. voc. sg., elided (σχέτλι’ = σχέτλιε): ’you reckless one!’
σός: σός — your, yours; possessive adj. (of σύ), masc. nom. sg.: ’yours’
σύν: σύν — with, together with; prep. + dat. · also adv. or preverb in tmesis, apart from its verb (σύν … ἄραξε ’would smash together’)
τήλεμος: Τήλεμος — Telemus, a seer; masc. nom. sg., proper name
τίπτ: τίπτε (= τί ποτε) — why ever, why then; interrog. adv., elided (τίπτ’ = τίπτε)
τίσατο: τίνω (mid. τίνομαι) — pay back, punish; aor. 3 sg. mid.: ’punished’ (Attic ἐτίσατο, unaugmented)
τυτθόν: τυτθός — small, little; neut. acc. sg. used as adv.: ’by a little’
φάσαν: φημί — say; impf. 3 pl., epic (= Attic ἔφασαν): ’they said’
φθεγξαμένου: φθέγγομαι — utter a sound, speak; aor. part. mid. masc. gen. sg., with τευ: ’of someone speaking’
χολώσατο: χολόομαι — grow angry; aor. 3 sg. mid., unaugmented (= ἐχολώσατο): ’grew angry’
ἀεικελίην: ἀεικέλιος — unseemly, shameful (Attic ἀεικής); fem. acc. sg.
ἀλλοτρίης: ἀλλότριος — of another, foreign, strange; fem. gen. sg.
ἀπέλεθρον: ἀπέλεθρος — immense, boundless; acc. sg. (here fem., agreeing with ἶν)
ἀπολοίατο: ἀπόλλυμι — destroy; mid. perish; aor. opt. 3 pl. mid., epic -οίατο (= -οιντο): ’they might perish’
ἀπορρήξας: ἀπορρήγνυμι — break off, tear off; aor. part. act. masc. nom. sg.: ’having torn off’
ἀπῆμεν: ἄπειμι — be away, be distant; impf. 1 pl., epic (= Attic ἀπῇμεν): ’we were away’
ἀστερόεντα: ἀστερόεις — starry; masc. acc. sg., with οὐρανόν
ἁμαρτήσεσθαι: ἁμαρτάνω — miss, lose (+ gen.); fut. inf. mid.: ’to lose’
ἄκικυς: ἄκικυς — feeble, powerless; masc. nom. sg., of uncertain origin
ἄραξ: ἀράσσω — strike, smash; aor. 3 sg., elided (ἄραξ’ = ἄραξε), with κεν: ’would have smashed’
ἄϊδος: Ἅιδης (Ἄϊς) — Hades; masc. gen. sg., epic Ἄϊδος (Attic Ἅιδου)
ἅζεο: ἅζομαι — fear, shrink from, revere; impf. 2 sg. mid., unaugmented, uncontracted (= ἥζου): ’you shrank (from)’
ἐδέγμην: δέχομαι — receive, await, expect; aor. (root form) 1 sg. mid., epic: ’I was expecting’
ἐδαμάσσατο: δαμάζω (δαμάω) — overpower, subdue; aor. 3 sg. mid., epic -σσ-: ’overpowered’
ἐδεύησεν: δεύω (= δέω) — lack, fall short; aor. 3 sg., epic (= Attic ἐδέησεν): ’fell short’
ἐθέλῃσ: ἐθέλω — wish, be willing; pres. subj. 3 sg., elided (ἐθέλῃσ’ = ἐθέλῃσι): ’he is willing’
ἐκέλσαμεν: κέλλω — drive a ship ashore, beach; aor. 1 pl.: ’we ran (the ship) ashore’
ἐκλύσθη: κλύζω — wash, surge, dash; aor. pass. 3 sg.: ’was dashed up’
ἐμπάζετο: ἐμπάζομαι — pay heed to, care for (+ gen.); impf. 3 sg. mid.: ’was heeding’
ἐννοσίγαιον: ἐννοσίγαιος — earth-shaker (epithet of Poseidon); masc. acc. sg. as a noun
ἐξαλαῶσαι: ἐξαλαόω — blind completely; aor. inf. act.: ’to blind’
ἐπέρεισε: ἐπερείδω — lean upon, press, put weight on; aor. 3 sg.: ’put (force) into it’
ἐπιδινήσας: ἐπιδινέω — whirl round; aor. part. act. masc. nom. sg.: ’having whirled’
ἐρήτυον: ἐρητύω — hold back, restrain; impf. 3 pl.: ’were holding back’
ἐρεθιζέμεν: ἐρεθίζω — provoke, rouse; pres. inf. act., epic -έμεν (= Attic -ειν): ’to provoke’
ἔβαλεν: βάλλω — throw, hurl; aor. 3 sg., ν-movable: ’threw’ (κὰδ … ἔβαλεν = κατέβαλεν ’threw down’)
ἔδμεναι: ἔδω — eat; pres. inf., epic -μεναι (= Attic ἐσθίειν): ’to eat’
ἔμελλες: μέλλω — be about to, be going to (+ inf.); impf. 2 sg.: ’you were going to’
ἠμείβετο: ἀμείβομαι — answer, reply; impf. 3 sg. mid.: ’answered’
ἠύς: ἠύς (ἐύς) — good, noble; masc. nom. sg., epic (Attic ἀγαθός)
ἧκ: ἵημι — send, hurl; aor. 3 sg., elided (ἧκ’ = ἧκε): ’hurled’
ἰήσεται: ἰάομαι — heal, cure; fut. 3 sg. mid.: ’will heal’
ἵησιν: ἵημι — send, throw; pres. 3 sg. (Attic ἵησι): ’sends, throws’
ἶν: ἴς — strength, force; fem. acc. sg. ἶν, elided in the text (ἶν’)
ὀδυρόμενοι: ὀδύρομαι — lament, mourn; pres. part. mid. masc. nom. pl.: ’lamenting’
ὀδυσεῦ: Ὀδυσσεύς — Odysseus; masc. voc. sg., single-σ form (Attic Ὀδυσσεῦ)
ὀκριόεντι: ὀκριόεις — jagged, rugged; masc. dat. sg. (-εντι), with μαρμάρῳ
ὀλέσας: ὄλλυμι — destroy, lose; aor. part. act. masc. nom. sg.: ’having lost’
ὀλίγος: ὀλίγος — little, small, puny; masc. nom. sg.
ὀρέγων: ὀρέγω — stretch out; pres. part. act. masc. nom. sg.: ’stretching out’
ὀτρύνω: ὀτρύνω — urge on, stir; pres. 1 sg. indic. or subj.: ’I urge’ / ’I may urge’, with an inf. of what is urged
ὦσα: ὠθέω — push, shove; aor. 1 sg., epic ὦσα (= Attic ἔωσα): ’I pushed (off)’

__broaden__.δόμεναι: δίδωμι — give; aor. inf., epic -μεναι, used as imperative: ’give’ · also inf. after ὀτρύνω, ’to give’ (πομπὴν ὀτρύνω δόμεναι ’I urge (him) to give a conveyance’)
__broaden__.κακῶς: κακός — bad, evil; adv.: ’wickedly, shamefully’ · also ’miserably, in misery’ (ὀψὲ κακῶς ἔλθοι ’may he come late, in misery’)
__broaden__.ἑὴν: ἑός (= ὅς, ἥ, ὅν possessive) — his own, her own; 3rd-person reflexive possessive adj., fem. acc. sg. ἑήν, agreeing with εὐνήν: ’his own (lair)’ · also agreeing with πατρίδα: ’his own’ (ἑὴν ἐς πατρίδα γαῖαν ’to his own fatherland’)
__broaden__.ἧκε: ἵημι — send, let go, let fall; aor. 3 sg. (with κὰδ in tmesis: ’let down’) · also of hurling a missile: ’hurled’ (ἧκε … κορυφὴν ὄρεος ’hurled the peak of a mountain’)
__broaden__.ὀφθαλμοῦ: ὀφθαλμός — eye; gen. sg. (with a verb of depriving: ’of his eye’) · also depending on a noun: ’of the eye’ (ὀφθαλμοῦ … ἀλαωτύν ’the blinding of the eye’)
__broaden__.ὡς: ὡς — as, how, that, when; with the optative introduces a wish: ’so may…’ (unaccented; accented ὥς / ὣς is ’thus’) · also ὡς + unaugmented ὄφελον + inf., an unfulfillable wish: ’would that...’ · also ὡς + opt., a purpose clause (= ἵνα): ’so that’ (ὡς τὸν χόλον ἐξακέσαιτο ’so that he might appease the anger’) · also exclamatory ὡς + adj. + inf.: ’how (good, etc.) it is to...’ (ὡς ἀγαθὸν ... λιπέσθαι ’how good a thing it is to be left behind’) · also plain ὡς + indic., ’as’ (ὡς σὺ κελεύεις ’as you command’) or ’how’ in an indirect question (ὡς ἐπὶ πόντον ἐλεύσομαι ’how I shall come upon the sea’) · also ὡς ἄν + subj., a purpose clause: ’so that’ (ὡς ἂν μὴ κλαίουσα κατὰ χρόα καλὸν ἰάπτῃς ’so that you might not mar your fair skin with weeping’) · also ὡς δ’ ὅτε introducing an epic simile, ’as when’, its clause taking indic. or ἄν/κε + subj. for a general case: ὡς δ’ ὅτ’ ἂν ... φανήῃ ’as when ... should appear’ · also comparative ’like’, placed after the noun it compares (ἀνέμου ὡς πνοιή ’like a blast of wind’) · also ὡς εἰ ’as if, like’ (ὡς εἰ πτερὸν ἠὲ νόημα ’as if a wing or a thought’) · also ὡς + ἄν + opt., potential, ’as, in the way that, such as’ (ὡς οὐκ ἂν ἔλποιο ’such as you would not expect’) · also introducing a simile with the subj. and no ἄν: ’as when (a woman weeps)’ · also in an asseveration with fut. indic., ’as surely as’ (ὡς οὐκ ὀφθαλμόν γ’ ἰήσεται ’as surely as nothing will heal the eye’)
